headline: This law lets the federal government accept donated land of about 160 acres to expand Yucca House National Monument in Colorado.
what_it_does: The Department of the Interior is allowed to take ownership of about 160 acres, plus any related interests in that land, if the owners give it to the government as a donation. Once the land is acquired, Interior must change the monument's boundaries to include it. The added land is then managed as part of the monument.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of the proposed addition land
who_it_affects.how: They may choose to donate their land or interests in it to the federal government, but the bill does not require any sale or transfer.

who_it_affects.group: National Park Service and Department of the Interior
who_it_affects.how: They must accept and manage the donated land as part of the monument once it is acquired and the boundaries are adjusted.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to Yucca House National Monument
who_it_affects.how: If the land is added, the monument's protected area would grow, which could affect how the added land is accessed and used.

when_it_takes_effect: The authority took effect when the law was enacted on January 13, 2021, but the boundary change happens only after the land is actually donated and acquired.
